articles.title: Polanski challenged over whether he thinks Israel has right to exist
articles.summary: The Green Party leader defends his decision to miss a debate on a controversial motion about Zionism which was passed by party members.
articles.body:
Green Party leader Zack Polanski has defended his decision to miss a debate at his party's conference on a controversial motion declaring Zionism a form of racism.

Questioned by presenter Nick Robinson on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, he denied deliberately avoiding the debate, saying he had been campaigning in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election.

The motion, which was passed by party members, defined Zionism as an ideology supporting an "ethnonationalist Jewish state" and backed a single democratic Palestinian state encompassing present-day Israel.

articles.title: Maraisa revela que vai se casar com Fernando Mocó | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantora falou sobre o casamento em vídeo publicado pela dermatologista goiana Ana Luiza Rassi e brincou que a amiga terá que preparar a noiva e o noivo.
articles.summary: Maraisa falou sobre o casamento com Fernando Mocó em vídeo publicado pela dermatologista goiana Ana Luiza Rassi. O casal está junto desde 2023.
articles.body:
A cantora Maraisa, de 38 anos, da dupla com Maiara, revelou que vai se casar com o empresário Fernando Mocó, de 44. A novidade foi mencionada em um vídeo publicado pela médica dermatologista goiana Ana Luiza Rassi. Em tom descontraído, a sertaneja disse que a amiga terá que preparar os noivos para a cerimônia (veja o vídeo acima).

No vídeo, Ana Luiza anuncia que um casamento está próximo e Maraisa entra na brincadeira, indicando que a médica terá uma tarefa especial na preparação do casal.

“Teremos um casamento em breve”, diz a dermatologista. “Vai preparar a noiva e o noivo”, responde Maraisa.

A cantora sertaneja e o empresário estão juntos desde 2023 e ficaram noivos no mesmo ano em que começaram a namorar.

A conversa foi publicada nas redes sociais e chamou a atenção dos fãs da cantora. No trecho divulgado, não foram informados detalhes sobre a data da cerimônia. O g1 entrou em contato com a assessoria de Maraisa para obter mais informações, mas não recebeu resposta até a publicação desta reportagem.

articles.title: 'Suplementos não tratam resistência à insulina e podem atrasar diagnóstico e tratamento', alerta Anvisa | G1
articles.standfirst: Agência alerta para vídeos nas redes sociais que recomendam substâncias como berberina, magnésio e mio-inositol para controlar a condição. Produtos não substituem acompanhamento médico.
articles.summary: Agência alerta para vídeos nas redes sociais que recomendam substâncias como berberina, magnésio e mio-inositol para controlar a condição. Produtos não substituem acompanhamento médico.
articles.body:
A Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) publicou nesta sexta-feira (9) um alerta sobre a divulgação de suplementos alimentares como alternativas para tratar a resistência à insulina. Segundo a agência, vídeos que circulam nas redes sociais recomendam substâncias sem comprovação científica suficiente para essa finalidade, o que pode levar pacientes a adiar a busca por diagnóstico e tratamento adequados.

Entre os produtos citados estão a berberina, o magnésio e o mio-inositol, frequentemente apresentados na internet como soluções para melhorar a ação da insulina no organismo.

A Anvisa ressalta que suplementos alimentares não são medicamentos e não podem ser comercializados com promessas de tratar, prevenir ou curar doenças.

O órgão também esclarece que o uso desses produtos não é necessariamente contraindicado para pessoas com resistência à insulina. Em determinadas situações, a suplementação pode ser recomendada por um profissional de saúde para corrigir deficiências nutricionais, mas não deve ser confundida com o tratamento da condição.

A resistência à insulina ocorre quando as células do organismo passam a responder de maneira menos eficiente à ação da insulina, hormônio produzido pelo pâncreas que ajuda a glicose presente no sangue a entrar nas células para ser utilizada como fonte de energia.

Como resposta, o pâncreas pode aumentar a produção do hormônio para tentar manter os níveis de açúcar no sangue dentro da faixa adequada.

Com o tempo, caso o organismo não consiga compensar essa resistência, a glicose pode se acumular no sangue, aumentando o risco de pré-diabetes e diabetes tipo 2.

A condição está frequentemente associada ao excesso de gordura corporal, especialmente na região abdominal, ao sedentarismo e a fatores genéticos. Também pode ocorrer em pessoas com síndrome dos ovários policísticos (SOP), entre outras condições.

Por que suplementos não devem ser usados como tratamento?

Segundo a Anvisa, suplementos alimentares têm a finalidade de complementar a alimentação e fornecer nutrientes ou outras substâncias em situações previstas pela regulamentação sanitária.

Isso não significa que sejam capazes de tratar alterações metabólicas ou substituir medicamentos prescritos.

A agência explica que produtos apresentados com finalidade terapêutica precisam atender às exigências aplicáveis aos medicamentos, incluindo o registro sanitário necessário para sua comercialização.

Assim, um suplemento não pode ser anunciado como tratamento da resistência à insulina, mesmo que contenha ingredientes estudados por possíveis efeitos sobre o metabolismo.

A Anvisa também alerta para o risco de que promessas divulgadas na internet levem pessoas a utilizar produtos por conta própria e deixem de procurar avaliação profissional.

Como é feito o tratamento da resistência à insulina?

O tratamento depende das características de cada paciente, das causas da alteração e da presença de outras condições de saúde.

De modo geral, a abordagem pode incluir mudanças na alimentação, prática regular de atividade física, controle do peso quando necessário e acompanhamento de fatores de risco metabólicos.

Em determinadas situações, medicamentos também podem ser indicados, especialmente quando existem doenças associadas, como pré-diabetes ou diabetes tipo 2.

A Anvisa reforça que a decisão deve ser individualizada e orientada por um profissional de saúde.

A recomendação é desconfiar de vídeos, anúncios e publicações que prometam normalizar a insulina ou tratar a resistência ao hormônio apenas com vitaminas, cápsulas ou fórmulas comercializadas pela internet.

Antes de utilizar qualquer produto com essa finalidade, é importante buscar orientação profissional e verificar se as alegações têm respaldo científico.

articles.title: Focos de calor quase quadruplicam no AM, e Manaus fica sob fumaça | G1
articles.standfirst: Seca agravada pelo El Niño faz queimadas em pastagens fugirem do controle. Em setembro, o Amazonas registrou 3.726 focos de calor, quase quatro vezes os 942 do mesmo mês de 2025.
articles.summary: Seca agravada pelo El Niño faz queimadas em pastagens fugirem do controle. Em setembro, o Amazonas registrou 3.726 focos de calor, quase quatro vezes os 942 do mesmo mês de 2025.
articles.body:
Manaus amanheceu nesta sexta-feira (9) mais uma vez coberta de fumaça. A Defesa Civil disparou um alerta nos celulares pedindo que ninguém saia de casa sem máscara, as escolas municipais fecharam e a prefeitura colocou a cidade em estado de atenção. O céu cinza da capital é a face mais visível de uma crise que se espalha pelo estado: em setembro, o Amazonas registrou 3.726 focos de calor, quase quatro vezes os 942 do mesmo mês de 2025.

O salto veio depois de um trimestre em que a chuva quase sumiu. De julho a setembro, Manaus acumulou 44 milímetros , uma quantidade ínfima perto dos 202 milímetros esperados para o período, segundo dados do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet). Agosto terminou sem chuva registrada, quando a média do mês é de 56 mm .

O ar que os moradores respiram mostra o tamanho do problema. Nesta sexta-feira, Manaus registrou a pior qualidade do ar do país segundo o Índice de qualidade do ar (AQI⁺), carregado de partículas liberadas pelas queimadas. Dentro da própria cidade, os bombeiros precisaram de um avião para conter um incêndio que já passava de 48 horas.

Fumaça de queimadas florestais encobre a cidade de Manaus. — Foto: EDMAR BARROS/ATO PRESS/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

Segundo o pesquisador Luiz Aragão, do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (Inpe), a origem do fogo segue um padrão conhecido nesta época do ano: queimadas para renovar pastagens e limpar áreas já abertas.

➡️ O que muda em 2026 é o cenário em que essas chamas são acesas. Com a floresta ressecada pela falta de chuva e pelo El Niño, o fogo escapa do controle e avança sobre a mata.

A proibição do uso do fogo em todo o estado só foi decretada pelo governo do Amazonas em 9 de setembro, quando agosto já havia fechado com 2.231 focos, acima dos 1.842 do ano anterior. O Ministério Público de Contas do Amazonas (MPC-AM) pediu uma investigação para apurar se as ações do governo estadual contra queimadas, incêndios florestais e episódios de poluição foram efetivas.

Defesa Civil recomenda uso de máscara em Manaus — Foto: Reprodução/Defesa Civil

Outubro é o fim da estação seca na Amazônia e, com ele, o auge da temporada de queimadas. É nesta época, antes da chegada das chuvas, que produtores usam o fogo para renovar pastagens, eliminar ervas daninhas e limpar a vegetação que volta a crescer em áreas já abertas.

Esse tipo de queima pode ser autorizado por órgãos ambientais, com limites de área. Porém, com a vegetação seca, as chamas ganham proporções que fogem de qualquer controle.

E isso se reflete nos números: os focos neste ano superam os de 2025.

Focos de calor no Amazonas — Foto: Infográfico/g1

Segundo Luiz Aragão, pesquisador do Inpe, o índice está pouco acima da média histórica e abaixo do registrado em 2024, ano em que a fumaça da Amazônia chegou ao Sudeste.

Hoje, os piores estados no ranking de focos de calor são:

O que agrava a situação no Amazonas é o contexto em que esse fogo acontece: uma floresta seca, sem chuva à vista, com incêndios muito próximos a uma capital.

🔴 E você pode se perguntar: se o desmatamento está no menor nível da série histórica, por que há tanto fogo?

Entre janeiro e junho, o Deter, sistema de alertas do Inpe, identificou 1.295 km² de áreas sob alerta de perda de vegetação nativa na Amazônia. É o menor patamar para o período desde o início da série histórica, em 2016.

O que Aragão explica é que a maior parte dos focos não está em áreas alvo de desmatamento, mas em pastos e áreas já desmatadas, muitas vezes na borda da floresta. Com a vegetação seca, o incêndio toma grandes proporções e fica difícil de controlar.

“Com a intensificação do El Niño, essas fontes de ignição que estão queimando nas áreas de pastagem, nas florestas secundárias, tendem a entrar nas florestas, que estão numa condição muito mais seca devido à falta de chuva. A somatória desses fatores é que gera esse aumento das queimadas e toda essa fumaça que atinge diretamente a população e a sua saúde”, explica Aragão, que atua na área de monitoramento ambiental por satélites.

Nesta sexta-feira, Manaus registrou a pior qualidade do ar do país, carregado de partículas liberadas pelas queimadas. — Foto: EDMAR BARROS/ATO PRESS/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

Com o alerta do El Niño e a seca na região, no entanto, especialistas apontam que o fogo deveria ter sido suspenso antes, o que não ocorreu. Após um agosto sem um dia de chuva e um começo de setembro sob chamas, o governo suspendeu o fogo com um decreto em 9 de setembro.

Após a medida, o Ministério Público de Contas do Amazonas (MPC-AM) solicitou que o Tribunal de Contas do Estado do Amazonas (TCE-AM) apure se as ações do governo estadual para combater queimadas, incêndios florestais e episódios de poluição atmosférica durante o período de estiagem em 2026 são suficientes e efetivas.

O g1 procurou o governo, mas não recebeu um retorno até a publicação.

De acordo com a análise do Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais (Cemaden), a umidade é baixa na região da Amazônia, com vários trechos sob seca severa e moderada.

Isso tem relação com a chegada do El Niño, aquecimento anormal das águas do Oceano Pacífico, que reduz as chuvas no Norte do país. Neste ano, o fenômeno é considerado forte, e a Amazônia central, onde fica Manaus, está entre as regiões mais sensíveis a ele.

Chuvas abaixo da média no Amazonas aumentam estiagem — Foto: Infográfico/g1

A última chuva na capital caiu em 3 de outubro, e não há previsão de nova precipitação. Cada dia sem água deixa folhas, galhos e capim mais secos, e é esse material que alimenta o fogo e o faz se espalhar.

E mais do que isso: a falta de chuva também impede que a fumaça se disperse e reduza o impacto na região.

“A atmosfera depende de dois grandes faxineiros: a chuva e o vento. Sob o El Niño, a seca predomina, e esses dois faxineiros praticamente entram em greve. O resultado é uma concentração maior da fumaça das queimadas. [...] O calor excessivo favorece a propagação do fogo, que fica mais descontrolado, e isso se soma à falta de chuva, que poderia reduzir a fumaça”, explica o meteorologista César Soares, da Climatempo.

Mapa mostra fumaça de queimadas no Amazonas — Foto: Infográfico/g1

Em 2024, quando grandes incêndios avançaram sobre a Amazônia, a fumaça “caminhou” por quilômetros e chegou a cobrir o céu de São Paulo. Em algumas cidades, houve registro de chuva escura.

De acordo com o meteorologista, desta vez ela não deve ir tão longe, por causa dos movimentos da atmosfera. Ainda assim, é possível que atinja estados vizinhos, como Rondônia e Mato Grosso.

Esse cenário, no entanto, só deve ocorrer caso o fogo piore na região.

Moradora de Manaus usa máscara para se proteger de fumaça de queimadas — Foto: EDMAR BARROS/ATO PRESS/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

articles.title: Meta proíbe anúncios do TikTok em suas plataformas nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: A proibição tem efeito imediato nos Estados Unidos, Canadá, Egito, Indonésia, Japão, Tailândia e Vietnã. Também vale para anúncios de outras empresas que direcionem os usuários ao TikTok ou a outros serviços da ByteDance nesses países.
articles.summary: A proibição tem efeito imediato nos Estados Unidos, Canadá, Egito, Indonésia, Japão, Tailândia e Vietnã.
articles.body:
Logotipo da Meta no Meta Lab, em Los Angeles, Califórnia (EUA), em 20 de maio de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Daniel Cole/Foto de arquivo

A Meta , dona do Facebook e do Instagram , proibiu anúncios da ByteDance, empresa chinesa proprietária do TikTok , em suas plataformas nos Estados Unidos e em outros seis países. A informação foi confirmada por um porta-voz da companhia na quinta-feira (8).

O TikTok se tornou um dos principais concorrentes da Meta na disputa por usuários, criadores de conteúdo e dinheiro de anunciantes.

A proibição tem efeito imediato nos Estados Unidos, Canadá, Egito, Indonésia, Japão, Tailândia e Vietnã . Também vale para anúncios de outras empresas que direcionem os usuários ao TikTok ou a outros serviços da ByteDance nesses países.

“Não temos obrigação de exibir anúncios de um concorrente cujo objetivo é tirar as pessoas dos nossos aplicativos”, afirmou a Meta. Segundo a empresa, recusar esse tipo de serviço a um concorrente é uma prática comum em diferentes setores.

“Continuaremos competindo pela qualidade dos produtos e pela experiência dos usuários”, acrescentou.

O TikTok e a ByteDance não responderam de imediato aos pedidos de comentário da agência Reuters.

Segundo o site do TikTok, a plataforma não permite links que abram outros aplicativos de redes sociais ou conectem os usuários às suas contas nesses aplicativos. Ainda assim, é possível colocar no perfil links que levem aos sites dessas redes.

A decisão ocorre em meio a outra cobrança da Meta ao TikTok. Desde agosto, a dona do Facebook e do Instagram pede que a concorrente e o YouTube adotem medidas semelhantes às que ela se comprometeu a aplicar para proteger adolescentes.

Naquele mês, a Meta fechou um acordo de até US$ 18 bilhões com estados americanos em um caso sobre danos causados pelas redes sociais a crianças.

A empresa concordou em estabelecer limites diários de uso do Facebook e do Instagram por crianças, restringir o acesso durante a noite e reforçar as medidas para impedir que elas vejam conteúdos inadequados para sua idade.

O TikTok não se manifestou publicamente sobre a cobrança da Meta. Em setembro, porém, fechou um acordo com o estado do Alabama para adotar novos limites de uso e reforçar a verificação de idade dos usuários no estado.

Esse acordo encerrou acusações de que o TikTok colocava crianças em risco e enganava os consumidores sobre a segurança da plataforma.

Nos Estados Unidos, o TikTok opera por meio de uma empresa controlada majoritariamente por investidores americanos. Essa estrutura foi criada após um acordo para proteger os dados dos usuários do país e evitar a proibição do aplicativo, usado por mais de 200 milhões de pessoas nos EUA.

A proibição dos anúncios pela Meta foi noticiada primeiro pela Bloomberg News, também nesta quinta-feira.

articles.title: Comércios do Acre são fiscalizados antes do Dia das Crianças | G1
articles.standfirst: Fiscalização do Procon segue até esta sexta-feira (9) nas cinco regionais do estado para identificar irregularidades e orientar comerciantes.
articles.summary: Fiscalização do Procon segue até esta sexta-feira (9) nas cinco regionais do estado para identificar irregularidades e orientar comerciantes.
articles.body:
Equipes do Procon-AC fiscalizam comércios durante operação que antecede o Dia das Crianças — Foto: Arquivo/Procon-AC

Os comércios do Acre estão sendo fiscalizados nesta semana que antecede o Dia das Crianças. A ação começou na última segunda-feira (5) e segue até a esta sexta (9), nas cinco regionais do estado.

A ação é feita pelo Instituto de Proteção e Defesa do Consumidor (Procon-AC). Segundo o órgão, o foco é identificar irregularidades e evitar práticas abusivas durante o período de maior procura por produtos infantis.

🛴🧸O Dia das Crianças é comemorado no Brasil em 12 de outubro. A data foi criada oficialmente na década de 1920, mas só ganhou força no calendário comercial a partir dos anos 1960, quando campanhas voltadas à venda de brinquedos ajudaram a popularizar a comemoração. Hoje, o período é marcado pelo aumento da procura por produtos infantis e pela tradição de presentear as crianças.

Durante as fiscalizações, as equipes verificam se informações importantes estão disponíveis ao consumidor antes da compra, como preços, condições de pagamento, promoções e políticas de troca.

Nos estabelecimentos que vendem brinquedos, também são observadas a indicação da faixa etária, as informações de segurança e a certificação dos produtos, quando exigida.

Ao g1 , John Lynneker, chefe da fiscalização do Procon-AC, disse que a ideia é evitar que problemas encontrados nas lojas prejudiquem o consumidor no momento da compra.

“O objetivo do Procon é esse: que o consumidor possa ir ao mercado de consumo com tranquilidade, com seu direito preservado e resguardado. A gente vai estar de olho, fiscalizando e acompanhando'', explicou.

Desde o início dos trabalhos, foram encontradas apenas irregularidades consideradas simples pelo órgão, como produtos sem preço informado e ausência do código do estabelecimento.

Conforme o Procon, os comerciantes foram notificados e corrigiram as pendências no momento da fiscalização. Além de verificar os preços, as equipes observam se as condições anunciadas nas promoções estão claras para o consumidor.

Também é verificado se há diferença de valor de acordo com a forma de pagamento e se essa informação está sendo apresentada de maneira adequada.

Consumidores que identificarem possíveis irregularidades durante as compras podem procurar o Procon-AC para fazer uma denúncia.

Segundo o órgão, o canal também fica disponível para situações em que o consumidor tenha algum problema relacionado às práticas comerciais verificadas durante a operação.

As denúncias podem ser feitas pelo telefone (68) 3223-7000.

articles.title: Quem é Navi Pillay, vencedora do Nobel da Paz 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Sul-africana de origem indiana, ela foi a primeira mulher não branca na Suprema Corte do seu país, presidiu o tribunal que julgou o genocídio em Ruanda e chefiou a área de direitos humanos da ONU. Nobel da Paz foi anunciado nesta sexta (9) em Oslo.
articles.summary: Sul-africana de origem indiana, ela foi a primeira mulher não branca na Suprema Corte do seu país e chefiou a área de direitos humanos da ONU.
articles.body:
Navi Pillay em 2014 — Foto: REUTERS/Ruben Sprich/Foto de Arquivo

A jurista sul-africana Navanethem “Navi” Pillay , de 85 anos, foi anunciada vencedora do Prêmio Nobel da Paz nesta sexta-feira (9).

Ex-chefe dos direitos humanos da ONU , ela foi a primeira mulher não branca na Suprema Corte do seu país, passou a vida dentro de tribunais e, ainda hoje, atua como juíza na Corte Internacional de Justiça (CIJ), no caso em que Mianmar é acusado de genocídio.

Pillay nasceu em 23 de setembro de 1941, em um bairro pobre de Durban. De etnia tâmil, um povo do sul da Índia com uma grande comunidade na África do Sul, ela é filha de um motorista de ônibus. Em 1965, casou-se com o advogado Gaby Pillay.

Conhecida como Navi, a sul-africana começou sua trajetória lutando em seu país contra o apartheid, o sistema de segregação racial que dividia a população por cor de pele e reservava a maior parte dos direitos políticos e civis à minoria branca.

O Congresso Nacional Africano (CNA), partido que liderou a luta contra o regime, formado por nomes como Nelson Mandela, a descreve como uma ativista anti-apartheid cuja trajetória se confunde com a história da libertação do país.

Com o fim do sistema, a carreira dela seguiu para fora do país. Pillay foi juíza do Tribunal Penal Internacional e, entre outros casos, presidiu o julgamento que tratou do genocídio ocorrido em Ruanda, na África, em 1994.

Também participou de decisões históricas que ajudaram a estabelecer que estupro e violência sexual podem configurar atos de genocídio e crimes contra a humanidade.

Ela atuou na corte por oito anos, incluindo quatro anos como presidente.

Navi Pillay em 2011, quando era Alta Comissária das Nações Unidas para os Direitos Humanos — Foto: REUTERS/Valentin Flauraud/Foto de Arquivo

Entre 2008 e 2014, Pillay ocupou o cargo de Alta Comissária das Nações Unidas para os Direitos Humanos, a principal autoridade da ONU dedicada a acompanhar violações cometidas por governos no mundo inteiro.

Em setembro do ano passado, na ONU, ela supervisionou a publicação de um relatório da Comissão de Inquérito que concluiu que Israel cometeu genocídio em Gaza e que altos funcionários israelenses, incluindo o primeiro-ministro Benjamin Netanyahu, incitaram esses atos – acusações que Israel considerou escandalosas.

Após o anúncio do Nobel, o escritório de direitos humanos das Nações Unidas saudou a notícia da vitória de Navi Pillay, reconhecendo sua longa trajetória de defesa dos direitos humanos.

"É uma notícia incrível, precisamos de mais dedicação e compromisso com os direitos humanos. Esperamos que isso incentive e continue a incentivar e inspirar outras pessoas a se manifestarem em defesa e promoção dos direitos humanos de todas as pessoas ao redor do mundo", disse Shabia Mantoo, porta-voz do departamento, a repórteres em Genebra.

Depois, o próprio chefe dos direitos humanos da ONU se pronunciou. Disse que a conquista de Pillay representa uma vitória coletiva para os direitos humanos e para todos aqueles que buscam justiça e responsabilização:

"O fato de a Comissão do Prêmio Nobel ter decidido conceder o prêmio a Navi Pillay é uma vitória coletiva para os direitos humanos, mas também para a busca por justiça e responsabilização neste mundo. É evidente que precisamos de mecanismos internacionais de responsabilização criminal, incluindo o Tribunal Penal Internacional, e é evidente que temos um sinal muito forte de que isso é absolutamente crucial no mundo de hoje".

articles.title: Feriado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida: veja o que abre e fecha em São Luís | G1
articles.standfirst: Comércio de rua e lojas de shopping poderão funcionar em horários específicos. Órgãos públicos e agências bancárias terão atendimento suspenso.
articles.summary: Comércio de rua e lojas de shopping poderão funcionar em horários específicos. Órgãos públicos e agências bancárias terão atendimento suspenso.
articles.body:
Rua Oswaldo Cruz, mais conhecida como Rua Grande, é o principal centro comercial de São Luís. — Foto: Divulgação/Fecomércio-MA

Por causa do feriado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, padroeira do Brasil, celebrado na segunda-feira (12), o funcionamento de serviços em São Luís terá alterações.

O g1 reuniu as principais mudanças nos horários de atendimento. Confira.

Na segunda-feira (12), não haverá atendimento nas repartições públicas estaduais e municipais em São Luís. Os serviços serão retomados na terça-feira (13).

Durante o feriado, serão mantidos os serviços considerados essenciais, como atendimentos de urgência e emergência, policiamento, fiscalização de trânsito e coleta de lixo.

O comércio de [São Luís]( está autorizado a funcionar na segunda-feira (12), segundo a Federação do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo do Maranhão (Fecomércio-MA).

As lojas de rua, avenidas, galerias e centros comerciais poderão abrir das **8h às 18h**. Já os estabelecimentos localizados em shoppings poderão funcionar das **10h às 22h**.

Segundo a Fecomércio-MA, os funcionários que trabalharem no feriado terão direito ao pagamento das horas trabalhadas com adicional de 100% sobre o valor da hora normal, além de uma gratificação de R$ 53.

As agências bancárias permanecerão fechadas na segunda-feira (12).

Segundo as regras bancárias para feriados, contas de consumo, como as de água, energia e telefone, e boletos com vencimento na data poderão ser pagos no próximo dia útil sem acréscimo. A orientação é verificar as condições específicas de cada pagamento.

Os clientes poderão utilizar os canais digitais dos bancos, como aplicativos e internet banking, além dos terminais de autoatendimento disponíveis.

Os shoppings de São Luís deverão funcionar normalmente durante o feriado, seguindo os horários previstos para a data. As lojas poderão abrir das 10h às 22h, conforme a autorização informada pela Fecomércio-MA.

Não haverá atendimento nas agências dos Correios na segunda-feira (12), em razão do feriado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida.

Os supermercados de São Luís funcionarão em horário normal na segunda-feira (12).

articles.title: Abusive ex admits murdering woman after she began new relationship
articles.summary: Lee Inglis had twice avoided prison for previous knife attacks on Stacey Hogg in Hawick.
articles.body:
A man with a history of domestic abuse has admitted murdering his former partner a day after learning she had begun another relationship.

Lee Inglis pled guilty at the High Court in Edinburgh to stabbing Stacey Hogg to death in her home in Hawick earlier this year.

BBC Scotland News has learned that the 39-year-old had twice avoided prison for previous knife attacks on the mother of three.

He was still serving a home curfew and an unpaid work order when he killed the 35-year-old in June.

He waited until his curfew ended at 07:00 before making the three-minute journey from his parents' home to Stacey's house.

Warning: This article contains details readers may find upsetting

The court heard that he slipped in through the back door and attacked Stacey as she came down the stairs.

She suffered "catastrophic wounds" to her neck and head. Police found her in a pool of blood on a downstairs bathroom floor.

The court heard that when he was arrested by police he told them: "I intended to cut off her head."

"If I couldn't have her, nobody would," he added.

Inglis will be sentenced at the High Court in Edinburgh on 5 November.

Inglis had a history of domestic abuse against his former partner.

He was sentenced to 150 hours of unpaid work in 2022 for assaulting Stacey and threatening to kill her with a kitchen knife.

Court records show he admitted injuring her by putting his hands around her neck and causing her to fall to the ground and strike her head.

He avoided prison again last year after being convicted of holding a knife to her throat and cutting her face.

He was sentenced to 200 hours of unpaid work, two years of supervision and a night-time home curfew.

The Border Telegraph, a local newspaper, reported that Sheriff Peter Paterson said at the time that the offence met the threshold for custody.

But he took into account the "complex family dynamic" and that the victim was opposed to a non-harassment order being imposed.

Stacey's death led to an outpouring of anger and grief in Hawick.

Her funeral service was moved to the town hall to accommodate the number of mourners and an online fundraiser to provide support for her children raised more than £45,000.

A family statement at the time described her as "a sister, a daughter, a mother and a friend who was taken from us far too soon.

"She was a cherished daughter, an amazing sister and a loyal friend who touched the lives of so many.

"Her kindness, strength and love will never be forgotten, and she will be deeply missed by everyone who knew her."

Det Insp Ross Duthie, of Police Scotland, said he hoped the outcome of the court proceedings brought some comfort to Stacey's family.

"This was a horrific incident which understandably caused a lot of concern in the local area, and I would like to thank the community for their patience and assistance throughout our investigation," he said.

"Inglis is a violent and dangerous individual who will now face the consequences of his despicable actions."

The case is one of a series of high profile violent crimes against women and girls in Scotland in recent months.

Stacy Hunter, 35, was murdered by her estranged husband, Jim Mair, at her home near Houston in Renfrewshire in July. His body was found nearby.

Three weeks earlier he had appeared in court accused of strangling her and was released on bail.

Her family say they saw clear signs she was being manipulated, controlled and abused by Mair , long before the murder.

Vicki Solomon, 44, died after being found seriously injured in a house in the East Craigs area of Edinburgh in July.

Her former partner Lee Grennan was charged with her murder and made no plea when he appeared in court. He was found dead at HMP Edinburgh a few days later.

The Police Investigations and Review Commissioner confirmed Police Scotland had been contacted before the fatal attack on the mother-of-two.

Meanwhile, police officer Alan Greer - who took his own life in May - was revealed to be a violent rapist who attacked and attempted to murder women over 14 years.

Police Scotland chief constable Jo Farrell said this week that 45 serving officers are currently suspended over allegations of violence against women and girls.

First Minister John Swinney has described violence against women and girls as a "national emergency".

He says he will introduce misogyny education in schools across Scotland and has confirmed a GPS tracking pilot for people on bail - including those accused of domestic abuse - will begin next year.

If you or someone you know have been affected by domestic abuse, you can find more information about organisations that can help at BBC Action Line.

articles.title: A hiker went missing on Arkansas' Eagle Rock Loop; a stranger took a day off to find him, and now his family has launched a GoFundMe to thank her
articles.summary: A missing hiker in Arkansas was found after a stranger took a day off work and joined the search with her dog, prompting his family to launch a GoFundMe
articles.body: A missing hiker in Arkansas was found after a stranger took a day off work and joined the search with her dog, prompting his family to launch a GoFundMe campaign to thank the pair. Matt Teeters disappeared on September 23, 2026, while hiking the Eagle Rock Loop in the Ouachita National Forest after becoming separated from his cousin. As search efforts continued overnight, Ashley Lea Smith, a local hiker familiar with the terrain, decided to look for him the following morning. Accompanied by her dog, Buckey, Smith eventually located Teeters near Winding Stair. He was reunited with his family after first responders checked him for injuries. His family later launched an online fundraiser to help pay for repairs and improvements to Smith's home.How a stranger and her dog found the missing hiker in ArkansasTeeters was hiking the Eagle Rock Loop near Albert Pike in Arkansas when he became separated from his cousin, Nick Walker, on September 23. According to local reporting, the pair were approaching Winding Stair, where a relative was expected to meet them with additional water and Gatorade.Teeters was walking behind Walker because his feet were blistered and he had slowed down. Walker reached the meeting point, but Teeters did not arrive. After searching the surrounding area without finding him, the family contacted authorities, and an emergency signal was sent using satellite messaging.The disappearance prompted a search led by the Montgomery County Sheriff's Office, with assistance from the US Forest Service. Search efforts continued into the night as rescuers worked to locate Teeters in the mountainous terrain.News of the missing hiker eventually reached Ashley Lea Smith, who was familiar with the area through her hiking experience. On the morning of September 24, she called in to work, took her dog Buckey and headed towards the Winding Stair area to look for him.Smith approached from Musgrove Hole and eventually spotted a man wearing a red shirt. In an interview with local television station KTHV, she recalled calling out to ask whether he was Matt.When he confirmed his identity, Smith told her dog, “Buckey, we found him.”Teeters was subsequently reunited with his cousin and family. Smith told KTHV that emergency medical personnel and other first responders examined him and found that he had scrapes and bruises. He was otherwise reported to be OK.Why the family launched a GoFundMe for the rescuerAfter Teeters was found, his family decided to organise a fundraiser to express their gratitude to Smith for taking the time to search for someone she had never met.The GoFundMe campaign, titled Giving Back to Ashley and Buckey - Hiking Heroes, was organised by Jennifer Teeters, Matt's sister. According to the campaign description, the family wanted to help Smith with repairs and improvements to her home, including work on the roof and the construction of a new deck.The family contributed the first $500 towards the cost of materials, labour and other expenses associated with the work. In its appeal, the family explained that Smith had provided the news they had spent the night hoping and praying for.The fundraiser was intended as a way to offer practical assistance in return for her kindness. Smith had not asked for a reward, and the family described the campaign as an opportunity to support someone who had stepped forward when they needed help.According to People, the campaign had raised more than $6,000 by October 2, 2026, towards its stated goal at the time. Fundraising totals can change, and the amount raised should be checked against the live campaign page before publication.Ashley Smith says she was simply trying to do the right thingDespite the attention surrounding the rescue, Smith played down the idea that she had done anything extraordinary.Speaking to KTHV, she said she did not consider herself special and described her decision as an attempt to help someone in need. She also credited Buckey for accompanying her during the search.Smith's actions came after an overnight search involving authorities and other searchers. Her familiarity with the area helped her decide where to look, and she eventually located Teeters near Winding Stair.The rescue also brought relief to Teeters' relatives, who had spent hours uncertain about his whereabouts. Jennifer Teeters wrote in the fundraiser description that the family would never be able to fully repay Smith for the relief she brought them.The campaign has therefore become more than a fundraising appeal. It is an attempt by a family to offer tangible support to a stranger whose decision to help made a lasting difference to them.What happened during the search for Matt Teeters?The Eagle Rock Loop is a roughly 27-mile hiking route in Arkansas' Ouachita National Forest. Teeters had set out on the hike with his cousin, and the pair became separated while making their way along the trail.According to accounts shared by the family and local reporting, Teeters took a wrong turn near a trail junction and became lost. Searchers worked through the night, with the rugged terrain complicating communications and the effort to locate him.The incident also prompted online speculation about whether the cousins had argued or whether Teeters had been abandoned. His cousin rejected those claims, and the available reporting indicates that the separation occurred during the hike.Teeters was eventually found on September 24, and the family was able to reunite with him after the search. The subsequent GoFundMe campaign shifted attention towards Smith and Buckey, whose contribution the family wanted to recognise.Where the GoFundMe donations will goThe fundraiser is intended to help cover improvements to Smith's home, particularly a new deck and roof repairs. Jennifer Teeters said the family wanted to support Smith in the same spirit in which she had helped them.The initial $500 contribution came from the family itself, with the online appeal inviting other people to contribute towards the remaining costs.The campaign's stated purpose is to fund the repairs and upgrades, rather than to provide Smith with a general cash reward.You use AI every day. articles.title: John Constable's The Hay Wain draws in 21,000 visitors to Ipswich
articles.summary: One thousand people visit Ipswich on the final day to see the painting, before its return to London.
articles.body:
The curator behind John Constable's Hay Wain painting exhibition said it was "phenomenal" that 21,000 people had been to see it.

Over the summer, thousands came to Christchurch Mansion to see the 1821 oil painting that had been on loan to Colchester and Ipswich Museums from the National Gallery, London.

The famous piece depicts a rural scene near the River Stour in Flatford, and on its final exhibition day on Sunday 1,000 people came to take a look.

Curator Emma Roodhouse said people had been left feeling "emotional and overwhelmed" by the work.

"We were inundated with visitors and amazing reactions from people who had never seen the painting before, from ages right the way to tiny babies to ninety-three-year-olds," she told BBC Radio Suffolk's Matt Marvel.

The Hay Wain is one of Constable's best known works, but despite capturing the Suffolk countryside it was actually painted in Constable's studio in London.

He had been born in 1776 in East Bergholt and during his career produced hundreds of paintings of the Suffolk countryside, many of the River Stour, which gave the area the name "Constable Country".

The Hay Wain has since been returned to the National Gallery with the help of a specialist art transport company, Roodhouse said.

"I've still not fully realised that it has all taken place, and we're now in the midst of planning our final Constable exhibition, so the fun doesn't stop," she added.

"Hopefully people will come back and we'll still keep talking about Constable for years to come."

The third and final instalment of the wider Constable exhibition runs from 24 October to 28 February, and highlights the artistic and cultural relevancy of his art today.

articles.summary: Britain’s Prince Harry fell into depression when he ​took a break from royal duties in 2019 before he formally stepped down, he told a videocast about grief, where he also discussed feeling “emotionally numb” after his mother died.
articles.body: Britain’s Prince Harry fell into depression when he ​took a break from royal duties in 2019 before he formally stepped down, he told a videocast about grief, where he also discussed feeling “emotionally numb” after his mother died. Harry, the ⁠younger son of King Charles III, has been open about his mental health struggles and how the sudden death of his mother Princess Diana in a car crash when he was 12 has affected his life. “I’d spent so ⁠long emotionally numb to a large ​extent because ⁠nobody told me joy was still allowed,” he said on a Masterclass videocast called “Redefining Grief: Building Resilience Through Loss”. He ⁠also recalled the stressful period in 2019 when tension with the rest ​of ⁠the royal family was ‌mounting, and he and his wife Meghan went to Canada for a six-week break to consider their future. “Being in Canada, away from ‌the stressful environment where presumably my body was ‌just pumped full of adrenaline, within two or three days, I experienced this adrenaline crash, something that I’d never experienced before,” he said, according to media reports. “It was ⁠as if I needed stress in order to get the adrenaline to make my brain function because I became useless around the house. “I actually slipped into depression for about two weeks and I felt like I couldn’t function without adrenaline.” Weeks after their break in Canada, Harry and Meghan returned to Britain where it was announced ‌that they would stop being working members of the royal ​family. Two months ago, the couple moved back to Britain ‌with their son Prince Archie, 7, ⁠and daughter Princess Lilibet, 5, after six years living in ⁠California. Campaigning to raise awareness of mental health issues is one thing Harry still shares ‌with his brother, heir-to-the-throne ​Prince William. The pair are ‌barely on speaking terms since Harry ​repeatedly publicly criticized his family in interviews and his memoir.

articles.title: Is Trump signalling a return to war with Iran after the midterms?
articles.summary: US media reports suggest he may be weighing strikes before the vote, but the president has ruled that out.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has said that he does not intend to bomb Iran again until the November midterm elections, even though several US media outlets have reported that the Pentagon has drawn up plans to relaunch attacks before that vote.

Trump has been accused of misdirection on the issue in the past. The US launched its initial attacks on Iran on February 28, as talks with Iran were ongoing and despite Trump saying just the day before that he had not made any decision. One year previously, the US struck Iran towards the end of Israel’s June 2025 12-day war, despite Trump saying he would announce a decision about attacks “in two weeks”.

Still, striking Iran ahead of the midterm elections would be risky for the administration as the war remains deeply unpopular with Americans.

Resuming the war afterwards may have less of a negative impact on Trump, who is not eligible to run for another term as US president anyway.

Here’s what we know about Trump’s plans.

In the past two days, The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and other publications have reported claims by unnamed officials that the Pentagon has drawn up plans to attack Iran before the midterms, if authorised to do so.

On Wednesday, US publication Axios cited US and Israeli officials saying the Pentagon has instructed US Central Command (CENTCOM) to prepare for imminent major combat operations. The Atlantic also reported along similar lines.

On Thursday, Trump posted on his Truth Social media platform that he will not order a resumption of strikes on Iran before November 3, when the US midterm elections will be held.

“I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition…we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd,” he said.

The president added that the US is presently “having productive discussions” with the Iranian side. However, that was also the case on February 28, the day the US and Israel first struck Iran, triggering the war.

Trump did not make any reference to preparing for potential military operations, nor did he provide more details on the state of talks.

Why might Trump be hesitant about resuming bombing before the midterms?

Trump and Republicans are worried about a voter backlash against the war at the polls. The US war on Iran is intensely unpopular domestically as Americans have had to grapple with surging prices of gas, food and other basic commodities because of the crisis in the Middle East.

Since the start of the war, surveys have shown that large numbers of Americans did not approve of striking Iran.

Now, about 65 percent of Americans say they “disapprove” of the way in which Trump has handled the Iran war overall, according to a Pew Research Center poll released on Thursday. Trump stated at the start of the war that it would go on for just a few weeks, however, it is now into its eighth month.

According to Pew, most Americans now believe the war will continue for at least another year. Even Republican or more conservative-leaning voters are growing more negative about the war, its poll found.

The conflict has also severely affected Trump’s personal ratings and eroded support for Republicans. A Reuters/Ipsos poll on Thursday found that only 30 percent of his supporters were enthusiastic about voting in the midterms, compared with 48 percent of Democratic voters.

About 13 percent of those who voted for Trump in 2024 say they are not sure who to vote for in the congressional elections.

Delaying attacks until after the elections could potentially shield Republican candidates from voter backlash, analysts say.

While analysts say Trump will see a good performance at the polls as approval for renewed strikes, a Republican defeat at the polls could equally further incentivise him to hit Iran again as he will calculate that he has little to lose at that point.

While that could further affect Trump’s ratings, the president is not eligible to run in the next presidential election in any case.

Will the US restart the war after the midterms?

In recent weeks, the US president has threatened to “end” the war with force after the elections as talks with Iran have dragged on.

At a Republican convention in September, he accused Iran of trying to affect the outcome of the midterms and said that conflict “is going to end immediately after the elections”.

In an interview with Time magazine two weeks ago, he also said it would be “possible” to ramp up bombing in Iran after the elections, but declined to elaborate. Analysts say his comments were designed to calm voters, while at the same time warning Iran of potential aggression after the vote.

Last week, the US military dispatched about 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines aboard several ships now sailing to the Middle East amid threats of new attacks from Trump. The vessel formation included the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group.

The deployment increases the number of US troops in the region to 20,000, alongside hundreds of aircraft and at least three carrier strike groups.

In the past, US troop build-up in the Middle East and the Caribbean has subsequently resulted in military action.

In June, Washington and Iran signed a ceasefire agreement that quickly broke down over control of the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump has repeatedly said that the US has the upper hand in the strait, citing more oil exports and Iran’s weakened economy. He has also voiced aversion to a deal with Tehran over management of Hormuz, but said he might consider it because “they’re willing to offer us anything to stop”.

Washington rejected a recent proposal from Iran to reopen the strait based on certain conditions it wants the US to meet, including the lifting of sanctions, unfreezing Iranian assets and guaranteeing an end to attacks. Last week, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran was considering a counterproposal from the US.

articles.body: Samaritan House, a nonprofit supported by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI), founded by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan, prepares approximately 3,000 meals each month for community members facing hardship in San Mateo County, California. Alongside its meal services, the organisation helps households struggling to afford groceries and other essentials. Its programmes support people grappling with rising living costs, including families whose incomes are stretched by housing costs and everyday expenses. Through food distribution and other community services, Samaritan House works to ensure that vulnerable residents can access essential support when they need it.How Priscilla Chan’s philanthropy supports local communitiesThe Chan Zuckerberg Initiative was established by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan to support work across science, education and community development. Through its community programmes, CZI funds local organisations working to address challenges affecting residents, including food insecurity, housing difficulties and access to essential services.Samaritan House has listed CZI among its major donors. The initiative is part of a wider network of supporters that helps the nonprofit sustain its services for people experiencing financial hardship. Its work demonstrates how philanthropic contributions can support organisations with established local networks and experience assisting vulnerable households.How Samaritan House helps people facing food insecurityFood insecurity does not affect only people without jobs. Working individuals and families can also struggle to afford nutritious meals when rent, transport, healthcare and other household expenses consume much of their income. Even a relatively small increase in living costs can leave some households with difficult choices about how to spend their money.Samaritan House provides food assistance through services that include grocery distribution and prepared meals. These programmes help people access food without having to meet the entire cost themselves. For families with children, such support can help ease pressure on household budgets and leave more money available for other essentials.The organisation also provides services beyond food assistance, including healthcare and housing-related support. This broader approach recognises that financial hardship rarely occurs in isolation. A household struggling to pay rent may also find it difficult to afford groceries, medical care and other necessities.Why community food programmes matterFood assistance can provide immediate relief to people whose incomes do not stretch far enough to cover essential expenses. Grocery support allows households to prepare meals at home, while prepared-food programmes can help people who have limited access to cooking facilities or face other barriers.For families dealing with high housing costs, these services can help free up part of a limited budget for rent, utilities, medicines, transport and children’s school requirements. They do not resolve the underlying causes of food insecurity, but they can help people manage immediate needs while navigating financial difficulties.Community food programmes also rely on coordination between charities, donors, volunteers and local residents. Donations can help organisations maintain their services, while volunteers contribute time and labour to prepare food, organise supplies and distribute assistance.The role of volunteers in fighting hungerVolunteers are an important part of many community food programmes. Their responsibilities can include preparing meals, packing grocery supplies, organising distributions and helping deliver food to people who cannot easily reach a distribution centre.For some volunteers, the motivation to help may come from personal experiences of financial hardship or food insecurity. Having faced similar challenges themselves, they may feel a particular connection to people who are now seeking assistance. Others contribute because they want to support their neighbours and strengthen their communities.Individual stories of volunteers who experienced food insecurity before helping others can offer a powerful human-interest perspective on the work of charities. Such accounts can show how personal experiences shape community involvement and how people who once needed support may later become sources of support for others.A community response to rising living costsSamaritan House’s food services form part of a wider effort to assist people facing financial hardship in San Mateo County. With support from donors, including CZI, and the contribution of volunteers, the organisation provides resources to residents who need help meeting basic needs.Its work illustrates the role local nonprofits play in responding to food insecurity, particularly when rising household expenses make it harder for people to afford groceries. For those receiving assistance, access to meals and food supplies can provide practical relief at a time when money is already stretched across competing demands.You use AI every day. And Michigan Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers debate gas prices and tariffs. Here’s what to know today. Hunger grips a rural community hit by Trump’s cuts In Dunlow, West Virginia, Bill Likens stared down a half-mile-long line of cars and trucks that started forming before the sun came up over the Appalachian Mountains. articles.title: Christa Pike is walking with help and eating after failed execution attempt, her attorneys say
articles.summary: Christa Pike has begun walking and eating again at a hospital a week after surviving Tennessee’s attempt to execute her with lethal drugs, her attorneys said.
articles.body: NASHVILLE, Tenn. — Christa Pike has begun walking and eating again at a hospital a week after surviving Tennessee’s attempt to execute her with lethal drugs, her attorneys said Thursday. Pike, 50, survived two doses of pentobarbital as the state sought to giver her a lethal injection eight days ago for the 1995 beating and stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. The drug didn’t kill her, and her arms were left burned and blistered, according to her lawyers. For the first few days of her hospitalization, Pike was unconscious and on a ventilator. Her first steps on Wednesday were “limited” and she required some assistance as she walked on Thursday, her lawyers said in a statement. She is also regaining mobility in her arms, and she was able to eat for the first time. But the lawyers warned uncertainty remains about her physical recovery and her legal standing after the attempt to carry out her death sentence. Questions remain about Pike’s recovery and legal case The failed execution on Sept. 30 has renewed scrutiny of how states carry out the death penalty. Texas on Wednesday carried out the first execution in the U.S. since the Tennessee attempt. “While her physical recovery has been remarkable, significant questions remain about the long-term effects of what she endured,” her attorneys said in Thursday’s statement. “Christa is dealing with the profound psychological trauma of having survived a failed execution, including the terror, pain and uncertainty of believing she was about to die.” Pike regained consciousness Tuesday and was able to speak after awakening, they said. They initially described her as “confused” soon after regaining consciousness, and said Thursday that she continued to struggle with concentration and memory. Doctors say it is too early to assess the long-term impacts, the attorneys added. It also remains unclear whether Tennessee will try to execute her again. Her attorneys have said that they will urge Republican Gov. Bill Lee to commute her death sentence to life in prison without parole. “She should never be subjected to another execution attempt,” they said in the statement. What went wrong with the execution remains unclear Lee has since postponed the state’s only other scheduled execution this year and ordered a review of why the execution failed. The state’s prison chief resigned after the execution attempt. Medical and lethal injection experts have focused on whether a problem with the IV line caused the drug to pool in her tissue instead of entering her bloodstream. Pike’s attorneys wrote in a court filing that “apparently at no point did any member of the execution team realize that the IV lines were not correctly placed.” State officials have offered no explanation of what occurred. As the process got underway Pike was asked if she had a final statement and she spoke of being at peace. About five minutes later, she raised her head and said her arm hurt. Later, she appeared to lose consciousness but could be heard breathing heavily until media witnesses were escorted from the witness room nearly 90 minutes into the execution. An ambulance took her to a hospital.

articles.title: Behind France's student riots: Communists, unions and a global propaganda network
articles.summary: A transnational pro-communist network funded by Neville Roy Singham is amplifying French student protests, seeking better schools.
articles.body: When young adults stormed France's Bastille on Thursday, a little-known media outlet called BreakThrough News sent followers a "BREAKING" alert: "French students flood Bastille Square in Paris." But that isn't the full story. A Fox News Digital investigation has found that a transnational network of far-left communist and socialist organizations is seizing on France’s fiery student protests to advance a wider political and ideological agenda, using tactics deployed in the United States over the past decade to amplify unrest, deepen divisions and project an image of chaos. Earlier in the week, BreakThrough News splashed another headline across the front of its website: "French students shut down schools in historic strike against austerity," mobilizing "with support from unions and progressive forces." But those "progressive forces" aren't limited to students demanding education reform as part of their "Lycéenne Mobilisation," or high school student mobilization. Only 1 of 3 is a Student or Youth Group From France to the United States, the United Kingdom, Brazil, Greece and India, adults with deep pockets are tapping France's school protests and turning a domestic education dispute into a platform for broader political and ideological confrontation. BreakThrough News is a pro-communist propaganda outlet based in New York City, funded by an American-born, Shanghai-based communist tech tycoon, Neville Roy Singham, who has financed a network of communist and far-left groups in the U.S. that have capitalized on grievances to stoke similar street unrest for almost a decade. A Fox News Digital investigation traces how a movement that the media is mostly framing as students protesting deteriorating school conditions is actually part of an extensive infrastructure of unions, communist activists, far-left political parties and international media organizations that are organizing demonstrations, calling strikes, mobilizing supporters and broadcasting the unrest around the world with "BREAKING" alerts. In a digital analysis of scores of news articles, social media posts and public statements, Fox News Digital has identified 50 organizations in the French student protest movement and its wider network of supporters and international amplifiers, revealing an activist ecosystem extending far beyond the students who launched the demonstrations. Of the network of 50 groups, 15 are student or youth groups, including several communist youth movements and a Muslim student association. The remaining 35 adult groups include a dozen labor unions; eight communist or socialist organizations; five groups spanning other issues from taxes to parental advocacy, environmental activism, economic justice, international media and diaspora organizing; five civil-rights or human-rights groups; four political parties, including La France Insoumise, or France Unbowed, and the French Communist Party; one Palestinian advocacy group that complete the "red-green" alliance of leftists with Muslims. FRANCE’S TEEN RIOTS TAKE EXPLOSIVE NEW TURN AS GOVERNMENT POINTS FINGER AT HARD LEFT 'Red-Green Ecosystem' of Socialists and Islamists The network stretches from French classrooms and labor federations to communist organizations in Greece and Britain and international socialist media outlets, such as BreakThrough News, demonstrating how a domestic education dispute has attracted organizations advancing broader political agendas involving capitalism, "austerity," policing, military spending and Israel. "What we're seeing here is the same Red-Green ecosystem that disrupts infrastructure choke holds in our country such as the Brooklyn Bridge, college campuses and congressional hearings," Mike Gonzalez, a senior fellow at the Heritage Foundation, told Fox News Digital. "And in the case of BreakThrough News, the same sugar daddy — Neville Roy Singham." The case offers a revealing look at the ambitions of France's revolutionary left. Even in a country with powerful labor unions, an established Communist Party, a substantial parliamentary left and a long tradition of street protest, these organizations are demanding political and economic changes that go well beyond the existing left-wing establishment. As one far-left environmental group, Les Soulèvements de la Terre, or "Earth Uprisings," declared in the midst of the riots, "Glory to the rebellious high school students." The statement invoked a call for broader political subversion: "Pour un soulèvement antifasciste" – "For an antifascist uprising." The network's amplification of France's protests illustrates how a local confrontation can be presented to international audiences as part of a broader struggle against Western governments and institutions. "The communist Red and the Islamist Greens have nothing in common but a common enemy, the Judeo-Christian, capitalist, free West, led by the U.S.," Gonzalez said. "Their goal is to dismantle us." The situation in France is potentially even more dangerous, according to Gonzalez, who cited the European nation's well-established and active communist parties and a history of government changing by street violence. He noted the fall of the Fourth Republic in 1958 after large protests over Algeria, and that the government nearly fell in 1968 over student protests. "And of course, there was the blood-drenched violence of the 1789 French Revolution," Gonzalez added. FRANCE ROCKED BY STUDENT RIOTS AS HUNDREDS ARRESTED, VIOLENCE SPREADS NATIONWIDE 'Right to Revolt' Since late September, politicians from the far-left political party, La France insoumise, were seen working with students organizing blockades in Seine-Saint-Denis, a low-income suburb northeast of Paris. French-Moroccan journalist Nora Bussigny wrote that "many elected officials" from La France Insoumise "have indeed worked to co-opt the student protests, at the risk of seeing them spiral out of control: by fanning the flames, discrediting institutions like the police, and legitimizing the principle of political violence." Soon after, a wide network of far-left groups put out the call for tens of thousands of secondary school students and supporters to march through Paris on Oct. 6, while demonstrations spread across France. Student organizations in the network of 50 include the Union Syndicale Lycéenne, or High School Students' Union; Union Étudiante, or Student Union; Fédération des Associations Générales Étudiantes, or Federation of General Student Associations; and Union Nationale des Étudiants de France, or National Union of Students of France, helped mobilize students for the Oct. 6 demonstrations. Other student organizations, including Solidaires Étudiantes, or Solidaires Students, have joined the broader campaign. The organizational machinery supporting the mobilization extends beyond the teenagers who first took to the streets. National labor federations and professional education unions have called on adult workers to join the mobilization, bringing the institutional reach of organized labor into the student movement. The Confédération nationale du travail, or National Confederation of Labour, declared: "The demands of high school students are also ours. They are right to revolt." The adult-led labor organizations in the network of 50 include: the Confédération générale du travail, or General Confederation of Labour; Force Ouvrière, or Workers' Force; and Union nationale des syndicats autonomes, or National Union of Autonomous Trade Unions. Several education-sector unions called for a strike and demonstration in support of the high school movement. The organizations include the CFDT Public Education, Training and Research; CGT Éduc'action; the National Federation of Education, Culture and Vocational Training–Workers' Force; SUD Éducation; and Syndicat National des Enseignements de Second Degré, the National Union of Secondary Education, affiliated with the Unitary Trade Union Federation. The support extends beyond teachers and students into a wider collection of organizations, including parents' associations, civil-rights groups, antiracist organizations and political movements. Among them are the Fédération des Conseils de Parents d’Élèves, or Federation of Parents' Councils; Ligue des Droits de l’Homme, or Human Rights League; Mouvement Contre le Racisme et Pour L'amitié entre Les Peuples, or Movement Against Racism and for Friendship Between Peoples; and SOS Racisme, or SOS Racism. TRUMP, WALTZ LINK FRANCE RIOTS TO MASS IMMIGRATION AS THOUSANDS ARE ARRESTED Communist Flags and Calls for 'Class War' In Paris on Tuesday, the big day of the protests, the ideological character of the mobilization was visible on the streets. In Paris, activists waved red flags of the far-left Fédération Syndicale Étudiante, or Student Trade Union Federation. Some demonstrators wore Palestinian keffiyeh scarves covering parts of their faces as they marched behind a bright red banner bearing the words "Contre Les Guerres Impérialistes," French for "Against Imperialist Wars." The slogan is a recurring political message among anti-war, feminist and revolutionary-left organizations. The message on the red banner continued, "Guerre De Clasee !" or "Class War!" over a bright yellow image of the hammer and sickle. The banner identified the Young Communists, associated with the Mouvement Jeunes Communistes de France, or Young Communists Movement of France, which works closely with the French Communist Party. Activists carried flags bearing the communist hammer and sickle. On Instagram, the organization announced the launch of "Democratic and Antifascist Vigilance Committees." "High school students neglected, pro-Palestinian activists persecuted, unionists fired. State repression against our democratic rights has intensified in recent years," the group declared. FRENCH SCHOOL RIOTS DEEPEN AS EXPERTS POINT TO FAR-LEFT ALLIANCE FUELING ‘BROADER CONFRONTATION’ 'Parti Communiste Français' At the protest, Fabien Roussel, national secretary of the French Communist Party, took photos with protesters and later posted a message on X: "Standing alongside high school students in Paris, together with Communist elected officials and activists." Red flags with white stars and the message "Parti Communiste Français" flapped around him. Online the French Communist Party has continued advancing other political campaigns, including a demand to stop supplying arms to Israel, under the slogan "Stop arming the Palestinian genocide!" On Wednesday, after the peak protests, the Nouveau Parti anticapitaliste – L’Anticapitaliste, "The New Anticapitalist Party," rallied supporters, declaring there are "always more reasons to mobilize." Other revolutionary-left groups, including Le Poing Levé, or The Raised Fist, and Révolution Permanente, or Permanent Revolution, have promoted solidarity between high school students and university activists. FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION Palestine Flags In Saint-Denis, where the protests began, the Parti des Indigènes de la République, or Party of the Indigenous of the Republic, shared a photograph of young men standing outside Lycée Paul Éluard, a high school that has become a symbol of the unrest. As red smoke billowed above them, the students stood in front of large gray letters spelling out the school's name, holding a Palestinian flag. The school was later featured in the New York Times under the headline, "The School Near Paris That Shows Why French Students Are Protesting." In the network of 50 groups, Étudiants Musulmans de France, or Muslim Students of France, rallied followers to protest for the right of youth to "study with dignity." And members of Urgence Palestine, or "Palestine Emergency," marched proudly in the student protests with the Palestinian flag. Elsewhere, French lawmaker Louis Boyard of the far-left party, La France Insoumise waved a Palestinian flag while standing at Paris-Est-Créteil University with students as they blocked their campus. In marches, their activists wave trademark purple flags that flutter with the group's acronym "FI" and a white φ symbol for the Greek word "phi." POWER COUPLE OF CHAOS: HOW A TYCOON AND ACTIVIST BUILT A 'REVOLUTIONARY BASE' AT THE HOUSE OF SINGHAM Singham Network Broadcasts France's Unrest On Wednesday, BreakThrough News published an article portraying the demonstrations as a "historic strike against austerity." It also published a dramatic Instagram video of Bally Bagayoko, the far-left mayor of Saint-Denis and a politician with La France insoumise, sliding in front of students during a confrontation with police. BreakThrough News described the scene as Bagayoko protecting "a line of French students from police as they attack the protesters." The anti-policing video received about 346,000 likes in one day. Among the accounts that liked the video were Twitch influencer Hasan Piker, a self-described Marxist; BreakThrough News editor Zoe Alexandra; the Houston chapter of the Party for Socialism and Liberation, the Pittsburgh chapter of Jewish Voice for Peace and other groups in the Singham network. Earlier this year, Piker traveled to Cuba as part of a far-left "caravan" supporting the island nation's communist government. There, he took a photo with Jodie Evans, Singham's wife and co-founder of CodePink, which has received $1.33 million from Singham. From Latin America, teleSUR, an international television network in the Singham network, frequently circulates material from left-wing media outlets, including BreakThrough News, and it shared footage of French students clashing with police. The video featured a dramatic soundtrack and the headline: "TENSIONS ESCALATE...." FRANCE’S VIOLENT STUDENT PROTESTS RAISE WARNING FOR AMERICA: ‘A CAUTIONARY TALE’ From France to Greece, India and the US As French students stormed the streets, the Communist Youth of Greece publicly expressed solidarity with their movement. "Victory for the struggle of the school students in France!" the group said in a statement. BreakThrough News quoted the Greek communist organization in its France coverage, describing the developments as "foreshadowing more student struggles to follow." Another international connection runs through Indian Alliance Paris, a small France-based organization of students, researchers and professionals who describe themselves as committed to a "democratic and egalitarian" India. In mid-January 2023, Indian Alliance Paris co-sponsored a teach-in in Manhattan, opposing the expansion of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. The venue: the People's Forum Inc., a midtown Manhattan hub for communist organizing that Singham launched in 2017 with $22.44 million in funding. Over the past near decade, leaders of the People's Forum have coordinated hundreds of protests across America's streets. The People's Forum co-sponsored the event with Democratic Socialists of America and other organizations in the Singham-funded activist ecosystem, including CodePink and the Party for Socialism and Liberation. In mid-May 2024, the People's Forum hosted a screening of a 1967 French film "La Chinoise," and described the film as a story about a small group of French students studying Chinese communist leader Mao Zedong, "trying to find out their position in the world and how to change the world to a Maoistic community using terrorism." Mao unleashed mass political persecution, violence, imprisonment and social upheaval in China. Attendees were invited to purchase an $8 "solidarity ticket." On Tuesday, Indian Alliance Paris promoted the French student agitation while drawing parallels with student demonstrations in India. It posted a message on X, sending a heart emoji "to Gen Z: In France. In India. Bravo for today." The result is a self-reinforcing cycle: far-left activist networks amplify protests around the world, then package the unrest as evidence of a growing global uprising. On Thursday, after the French students had headed home after their siege on Bastille, BreakThrough News posted a collage on Instagram of short video clips from the U.S., Spain, India, France, Brazil, Belgium, Chile and Germany with youth waving communist flags, clashing with police and flooding the streets. It posted a headline in bold capital letters over the videos: "YOUTH RISE UP AROUND THE WORLD." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: Satire silenced: Indian artists face censorship as anti-Modi protests grow
articles.summary: New Delhi accused of silencing dissent as satirical content and online critiques are removed under new rules.
articles.body:
New Delhi, India – Stand-up comic Brijesh Jha posted a parody video on Instagram last week to protest the removal of his name, along with his father’s and sister’s, from a voter list in the eastern Indian state of West Bengal.

The video, which alleged that India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had disenfranchised millions of voters at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), garnered 1.7 million views after it was posted on September 29.

Two days later, Meta, the United States-based company that owns Instagram, took the video down, citing “local laws” without giving further explanation.

“I felt very helpless that day. I have only one thing in this country – that I can vote. If you take that away from me, then I have nothing left. So I didn’t know what to do. As an artist, I can just make art, or I can protest,” the Mumbai-based artist told Al Jazeera.

Jha said his parody song was removed because the Modi government is “scared” after an investigation by the Indian Express newspaper last month revealed that two of the election commission’s three members had raised serious concerns over a controversial revision of voter rolls being conducted by the poll panel across the country.

The exercise, known as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), was launched in June last year to identify deceased, duplicate or dubious voters and remove them from the rolls. So far, the process has deleted more than 130 million voters – nearly 14 percent of India’s total voters, an overwhelming number of them Muslims who do not usually vote for Modi’s Hindu nationalist party.

The Indian Express investigation found that two of Kumar’s fellow election commissioners had formally objected at least 14 times to key decisions linked to the SIR exercise taken by their chief.

Opposition politicians and critics accused Kumar, a Modi government appointee, of acting at the behest of the BJP and demanded an independent inquiry into the decisions taken by the election commission during his tenure.

The revelations have led to street protests across India, demanding Kumar’s resignation.

On Tuesday, police in the capital New Delhi briefly detained the main opposition leader, Rahul Gandhi, and other leaders of his Congress party as they tried to march to the election commission office.

“The country has been hijacked by Narendra Modi through vote theft,” Gandhi told reporters. “What has been done to our country is called treason. Nobody is going to escape.”

In response, the BJP accused the opposition parties of “making a concerted effort to change the government”.

“They are deliberately attacking India’s democracy and constitutional institutions,” a BJP spokesman told reporters on Tuesday.

The Congress protesters and their political allies were back on the streets on Wednesday. Their demonstrations followed a series of protests by the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and a group of left-wing students in Mumbai and New Delhi since October 2. The CJP has planned another demonstration in New Delhi on October 10 if Kumar does not resign by then.

What stood out in these protests was an increasingly inventive language of dissent, driven by humour, art and music, with much of it existing online alongside the demonstrations on the streets.

But a crackdown on such memes and jokes has also been simultaneous.

According to the Indian Express newspaper, the government issued nearly 195,000 content-blocking orders to Instagram, Facebook and YouTube between March and July this year – an average of one blocking order every 68 seconds.

Rejecting the newspaper report, the government said in a statement, “With 600 million users in India posting up to 78,703 items every 68 seconds, it is reasonable to expect that on average, one of these items may not be lawful.”

The crackdown came after the Modi government tightened rules governing online content in February. According to the new rules, social media platforms must remove content that a government authority or court has declared “unlawful” within three hours of receiving the order, down from 36 hours previously.

Among those whose works were taken down was political cartoonist Satish Acharya.

Several of Acharya’s cartoons, some up to three years old, were removed and his Instagram account was blocked in India from September 28 until late on October 5, he told Al Jazeera.

“At different phases of history, people used cartoons as a tool to express their protest and question the people in power. With the advanced use of social media, cartoons appear in different forms now, sometimes memes and reels,” the 55-year-old said.

“I have a lot of hope in Gen Z. They are fearless, they are creative and they care for the country. Our politicians can learn a lot from them.”

Stand-up comic Jha, who attended the CJP’s protest in Mumbai, agrees. “The more cruel the power is, the softer, more humorous and more artistic the protest becomes,” he told Al Jazeera.

But Jha has refused to apply for a reinstatement of his name in the voters’ list.

“I think they will see this interview and probably I will be in some detention centre. I just want to see what will happen. I’ll not register my name again,” he said.

However, he had a satirical message for Modi as he urged the Indian leader to stop the crackdown on online content.

“Please give back my right to vote. You are a great leader with a 56-inch chest. You shouldn’t be scared of one video,” he said, invoking a long-held right-wing boast about Modi’s famous bust.
