articles.title: ‘A Ceuta-style surge is possible’: Border tensions on NATO’s eastern flank
articles.summary: Belarus-linked incidents trouble Latvia and Lithuania, where experts warn of security challenges.
articles.body:
Masked and armed men attempted to cross into Latvia from Belarus alongside 20 undocumented migrants on Monday.

“The (masked) escorts of the illegal migrants, who were located on the Belarusian side, were armed, issued threats to … soldiers, and also actively urged and drove the migrant group toward Latvia,” Janis Dombrava, Latvia’s interior minister, said on Tuesday.

Later, masked men managed to enter Latvia, destroying an electrical box and stealing surveillance cameras before returning to Belarus – an act of sabotage orchestrated by the country, according to Latvian officials. It was not clear if the second incident involved the same masked men as the first.

“Unlike many previous incidents, this time the provocation was particularly demonstrative and aggressive,” said Dombrava.

Since 2021, Belarus, Russia’s ally, has used migration as a tool to destabilise NATO’s eastern flank. It shares borders with Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia – the latter considered Europe’s weakest link.

“The crisis at the EU [European Union] border with Belarus has been ongoing for five years. The situation in Latvia has been deteriorating since May of this year,” Bartosz Chmielewski, Baltics expert from the Poland-based Centre for Eastern Studies told Al Jazeera. “There has been a steady rise in border violations and the number of people crossing.”

In September and October, “the number of border violations has already reached 12,000, a level equal to the total for the entire previous year”, he said.

According to Olevs Nikers, the Latvian president of the Baltic Security Foundation, “A Ceuta-style surge is physically possible, and we should plan for it.”

He was referring to the recent crossing of tens of thousands of people from Morocco to Spain.

“But sustained low-level pressure may be the more effective strategy. It creates exhaustion, budget pressure and friction between allies. Poland’s renewed controls on its border with Lithuania are already an example of this.”

He noted that Lithuania’s border with Belarus is four times longer than Latvia’s 173km (107 miles), yet pressure has been concentrated in Latvia.

“This looks less like spontaneous migration than a deliberate instrument, adjusted to test the neighbour perceived as most vulnerable,” Nikers said.

Any migration pressure from Belarus may cause bureaucratic chaos. Latvia, with a population of 1.8 million, would struggle with the reception, processing and providing medical aid to potential asylum seekers, he said.

According to the Polish Border Guard, in 2021, almost 40,000 people tried to cross the border from Belarus. Thousands more crossings of undocumented people were never recorded.

Before Russia’s war in Ukraine began in 2022, Belarus built a system – including travel agencies, plane connections and visa programmes – encouraging migrants seeking a better life to cross into the European Union from the east. The scheme targeted people from the Global South, or Latin America, Africa and much of Asia.

According to experts, the system has since been dismantled, but Belarus is still pressing migration when it can.

“A sudden influx of several thousand people into Latgale in winter would become a humanitarian and political problem before it became a border-security problem,” Nikers added.

Out of all of NATO’s eastern flank countries, Latvia seems the least prepared for provocations coming from the east.

“Until now, Latvia remained on the sidelines, as the pressure was primarily focused on Poland and Lithuania. Now it finds itself in the spotlight, partly because it is unprepared, its border infrastructure is inadequate, and the resources of the border guard – even with military support – are dwindling,” Chmielewski said.

“Latvia struggles to execute major infrastructure projects … It shares the shortest border with Belarus, but has been unable to complete the necessary infrastructure there; this is due both to the challenging terrain and the state’s limited operational capacity.”

Other experts said the migration pressure from Belarus might be a response to recent political developments in Latvia.

“The elections in Latvia were won by a coalition led by [Prime Minister] Andris Kulbergs, which seeks to maintain sanctions against Belarus. So Belarus uses both carrots and sticks to show it can destabilise the situation in the Baltics,” said Marta Jaroszewicz, assistant professor at the University of Warsaw’s Centre of Migration Research.

“For the past year, there have been periodic releases of Belarusian political prisoners, a process supported by the US administration. Belarus’s goal is the lifting of sanctions and the ability to transport its raw materials via Baltic ports, including through Poland. The objective is, in fact, the normalisation of trade.”

Russian and Belarusian pressure on the EU has also changed over the years as migration pressure is only one of the tactics employed. Others include disinformation, arson, the recruitment of local citizens and GPS jamming, according to Nikers.

He said that “2026 is increasingly about airspace and infrastructure. The most important change is that Russia has moved from targeting what we believe to targeting what we depend on: cables, grids, navigation and airspace. It is also increasingly operating below the Article 5 threshold.”

Established in the aftermath of World War II, NATO’s collective defence commitment, Article 5, was designed to ensure mutual protection among member states in response to the perceived threat of Soviet expansion, particularly in Eastern Europe during the early stages of the Cold War.

“This is an attempt at intimidation by Russia. And what deters Russia from aggressive actions on the eastern flank is the solidarity of European nations,” Chmielewski said. “That is what Russia fears most: that should it stage a more brazen provocation, solidarity will stretch from Lisbon to Stockholm, and the European Union will act as a united front.”

articles.title: DHS defends ICE shooting in NYC, says officers believed they were in danger
articles.summary: The shooting prompted protests in New York City and Mayor Zohran Mamdani condemned the incident.
articles.body:
The United States Department of Homeland Security has defended Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) shooting of a man in New York City while his child was present. Federal officials used the incident to criticise sanctuary-city policies that limit cooperation with federal immigration authorities.

New York officials have condemned the shooting and have called for ICE to end its operations in the city.

The shooting took place on Thursday afternoon when ICE officers attempted to arrest a man identified by New York City police as Oscar Belgal.

Homeland Security officials gave their account of the incident on Friday during a news conference, saying that Belgal refused to exit his car when approached by officers and then accelerated, striking two ICE vehicles.

They said officers then opened fire, grazing Belgal’s neck while his five-year-old child was in the back seat.

According to Homeland Security officials, Belgal received first aid and was taken to hospital before being transferred to a secure detention facility outside New York state. They did not disclose where Belgal is being held.

Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that the agents did not know the child was inside the vehicle when they fired.

ICE senior official Marcos Charles said agents had attempted to arrest Belgal as part of an investigation into suspected gang involvement in an earlier shooting of a US Customs and Border Protection officer.

According to US officials, Belgal is an undocumented migrant from the Dominican Republic who had previously evaded arrest and received a five-year sentence for grand larceny in April 2025.

“[Belgal] was a thug,” Mullin said at the Friday news conference. “The absolute worst of the worst.”

Mullin confirmed that officers were wearing body cameras but the footage has not been made public. New York City police released bodycam footage on Friday of police officers on the scene who had responded to a 911 call about the incident.

In other violent incidents involving federal immigration officers, video evidence has contradicted initial accounts from ICE and Homeland Security officials, including in Minneapolis, where footage of the fatal shootings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good challenged federal officials’ descriptions of the encounters.

The latest shooting prompted protests on Thursday night in the Bronx, where the shooting took place, with demonstrators condemning ICE and calling for the agency to be abolished. Tensions rose after NYPD officers clashed with some of the protesters.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani condemned the shooting and said he had called US President Donald Trump to demand an end to ICE enforcement in the city.

Speaking to reporters late on Thursday at the scene of the shooting, Mamdani said he had tried unsuccessfully to secure Belgal’s release in phone calls with Trump and Mullin.

“These actions are making the city less safe,” Mamdani said. “ICE is rotten to its core.”

Mullin accused Mamdani of prioritising politics over public safety and said Trump had offered to transfer Belgal to New York police custody if they pursued charges. Mullin said Mamdani refused this offer.

articles.title: 'Unprecedented security': How Delhi is bracing for October 10 protests against CEC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi is gearing up for major portests on Saturday as the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) plans to march to Jantar Mantar demanding the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi is gearing up for major portests on Saturday as the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) plans to march to Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. With police refusing permission for the demonstration, authorities have stepped up preventive measures across the national capital to stop protesters from assembling at unauthorised locations.The security arrangements include the deployment of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel, the temporary suspension of mobile internet services within a four-kilometre radius of the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing, and restrictions at 57 Delhi Metro stations. Police have also intensified checks at the city's borders, railway stations, bus terminals, hotels and other sensitive locations amid expectations of a large mobilisation.Delhi Police expects around 7,000 protesters to arrive in the capital, news agency ANI reported. More than 35,000 police and paramilitary personnel are expected to be deployed, according to sources cited by ANI. More than 120 companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) are also expected to be involved in the security arrangements.The Delhi Police commissioner has directed personnel to maintain restraint and professionalism, avoid reacting to provocation and prevent unauthorised gatherings. Officials have also been instructed to detain people attempting to stage demonstrations, regardless of their location. Why Delhi Police denied permissionJoint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said on Friday that permission had been denied for the October 10 demonstration, citing the short notice given for the event and concerns over compliance with directions during an earlier protest.The application was submitted on October 7, just three days before the proposed gathering. Police said applications for such demonstrations must be submitted at least 10 days in advance. Authorities also cited concerns arising from the conduct of an earlier demonstration in July.Despite the denial, CJP's Abhijeet Dipke reiterated that the organisation would proceed with its planned protest at Jantar Mantar. Several student outfits and political groups are also expected to join the mobilisation.AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal appealed to people across the country to participate, accusing the BJP-led government at the Centre of undermining democracy through alleged manipulation of electoral rolls."I appeal to all the people across the entire country that the way the BJP government at the Centre is playing with our democracy, people's votes are being deleted on a mass scale. Those who don't vote for the BJP have their votes deleted, while fake votes are added. This was happening openly under Gyanesh Kumar,” Kejriwal told reporters. Internet blackout, metro restrictions and border checksThe Union home secretary has authorised the temporary suspension of all mobile internet services within a four-kilometre radius of the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing, from 10pm on October 9 to 10pm on October 10. The restriction covers all mobile internet technologies, while services elsewhere in Delhi are expected to remain unaffected.Entry and exit gates at 57 metro stations will remain closed from 9pm on Friday until further notice. Interchange facilities will continue at affected stations, except New Delhi metro station. Among the stations affected are Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, Patel Chowk, Kashmere Gate, Janpath, Mandi House, ITO and Supreme Court.Several train services scheduled to arrive at or depart from New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4am and 2pm on Saturday have also been reported cancelled.Other preventive measures include:Deployment across Central Delhi: The New Delhi district has been divided into 20 zones, each to be monitored by senior police officers. Additional women personnel from Uttar Pradesh and Haryana have also been called in.Surveillance and monitoring: Police will use facial recognition systems, additional CCTV cameras, rooftop spotters and drones. More than 200 content creators are reportedly under scrutiny over online mobilisation linked to the protest.Checks across the capital: Police have stepped up surveillance at borders, hotels, guest houses, railway stations, bus terminals and airport approach roads. Vehicle restrictions in New Delhi may also be imposed depending on the security assessment.Detention arrangements: Six designated centres, including Chhatrasal Stadium, Rajiv Gandhi Stadium and Yamuna Sports Complex, have been identified to hold detained protesters.Liquor shops across Delhi have also been ordered to remain closed on October 9 and 10 as a preventive measure. Police told to exercise restraintDuring a briefing, the police commissioner instructed personnel not to react to provocative behaviour or engage in unnecessary verbal confrontations. Officials were also warned against situations in which their interactions with protesters could be recorded and circulated online.Unlike the deployment during the INDIA bloc protest, police teams have now been authorised to carry lathis or batons. CAPF units have been instructed not to issue weapons for the deployment, with letters sent to the concerned directorates regarding the arrangements.Senior officers will remain available on the ground to respond to developments. Police have also said that any proposal to shift the demonstration to Ramlila Maidan would require a separate application and a decision by the authorities.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: JMC cleanliness drive faces criticism over worker shortage
articles.summary: Jaipur JMC’s ward-wise Diwali cleanliness drive draws criticism over sanitation worker shortages, disrupting routine cleaning amid a hopper workers’ strike.
articles.body: Jaipur: A ward-wise cleanliness campaign launched by Jaipur Municipal Corporation has sparked criticism from Congress councillors in the Kishanpole zone, who argue that concentrating sanitation workers in a single ward is disrupting regular cleaning services in other areas.The campaign was inaugurated by Mayor Sunil Kothari in Ward 112 Thursday, with sanitation workers from across the Kishanpole zone deployed for the drive. The next phase is scheduled to be held in Ward 104 on Saturday, and workers from different wards in the zone have already been directed to participate.Mohammad Zakariya, councillor from Ward 114, welcomed the initiative but expressed concern over its impact on routine sanitation work elsewhere.“The campaign is a positive step, but it should not result in neglect of cleanliness in other wards,” he said. He suggested that the civic body either increase the number of sanitation workers or ensure sufficient staff strength is maintained in every ward so that regular cleaning operations are not affected during the drive.Councillor Sunita Methi also raised concerns over the shortage of sanitation staff in her ward. “Our ward already has sanitation problems. Taking workers away from here is completely wrong,” she said.The cleanliness drive is also facing challenges amid a strike by hopper workers in Kishanpole zone, which has affected waste collection.Niharika Sharma, deputy commissioner of Kishanpole zone, said the state govt was in the process of recruiting sanitation workers. “We will ensure that sanitation in other wards is not affected because of this campaign,” she said.The civic body now faces the task of carrying out its special cleanliness drive while maintaining routine sanitation across the zone.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Jaipur | Silver Rate in Jaipur | Bank Holidays in Jaipur | Public Holidays in Jaipur | Jaipur AQI | Weather in Jaipur | Petrol Price in Jaipur | Diesel Price in Jaipur | CNG Price in Jaipur | LPG Price in JaipurStay updated with the latest Jaipur news. articles.title: Patna HC orders production of Buddha Colony land records
articles.summary: Patna High Court orders original Buddha Colony land acquisition records produced by Oct 30 amid petition alleging unauthorised construction and encroachment.
articles.body: Patna: Patna High Court directed production of original records relating to the acquisition of land for residential purposes in the Buddha Colony area of the state capital, while hearing a petition alleging unauthorised constructions on 30 acres of the acquired land.A single bench of Justice Purnendu Singh passed the order on Friday while hearing a writ petition filed by Buddha Colony Grih Nirman Samiti.The petitioner’s counsel, Vikas Kumar, submitted that 60 acres of land had been acquired, of which 30 acres was given to Patna Municipal Corporation (PMC). He alleged that unauthorised constructions had come up on the land, adding that a large stretch of land near Buddha Colony police station, earmarked for a public park, had been encroached upon.The court directed the additional chief secretary of the state urban development department to ensure that the original acquisition records were produced by Oct 30. articles.title: CM’s ‘friendship’ pitch pays off as Muslim-majority Rejinagar gives BJP big win
articles.summary: BJP wins Rejinagar bypoll in Murshidabad, a Muslim-majority seat, as Shankharavh Sarkar beats AJUP’s Golam Nabi Azad by 75,816 votes.
articles.body: Rejinagar: BJP’s victory in the Rejinagar bypoll, a constituency with a nearly 72% Muslim population, on Friday, signalled a shift in Bengal’s conventional electoral arithmetic in which Muslims have traditionally stayed away from the saffron party.BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar secured 1,29,914 votes, beating his nearest rival by a margin of 75, 816 votes. AJUP candidate Golam Nabi Azad, who came in second, secured 54,098 votes.Sarkar described his victory as a “rebuke to communal politics” and Muslims “siding with development”. “They (Muslim voters) answered CM Suvendu Adhikari’s call and showed they stand with the state govt,” he said.He added that voters wanted bridges, hospitals and industrial parks and the CM had led the party’s engagement with the minority community.The CM, who announced a series of development projects in Rejinagar on Friday and laid the foundation stone for the Narkelbari bridge, said Muslim women had supported BJP because they had benefitted from the Annapurna Yojana.Of the 15 candidates in the fray in Rejinagar, 10 were Muslim — though the RSP candidate withdrew at the last minute for not being allocated its symbol.Congress candidate Abdullahil Kafi won 6,168 votes, Mamata TMC’s Rabiul Alam Chowdhury won 3,847, CPM’s Md Sayeed 3,797 and Democratic TMC’s Safiuzzaman Saikh 2,044.Humayun Kabir’s son Golam Nabi Azad’s defeat showed the limits of political legacies. Merely five months ago, Kabir had won 1,23,536 votes in the same assembly segment.A dejected Kabir said he wanted to step away from politics and move to Dubai with a Golden Visa because he was “mentally exhausted”.“Ever since childhood, I never tolerated injustice. I grew up protesting wrongdoing. Now I am 64, going to turn 65. I want to spend the final days of my life in peace in Dubai,” Kabir said.“I will enjoy good food, travel, take in the sea breeze and eventually be buried there,” he added.Reflecting on the current political landscape, he said, “I can’t deal with such oppressive and tyrannical people anymore.
